sections.title: Design Studio II
sections.description: This studio explores urban architecture as an embodiment of cultural values . Analytical techniques for representing urban conditions are explored extensively . Students are challenged to interact with large, complex programs , individually determining one large component of the assigned program. Siting, enclosure of space and dimensions of public space and commons are stressed in order to challenge students to project relevant and inventive architectural situations . Large scale site and ground plans are stressed in the development of the project.

sections.title: Design Studio II
sections.description: This course is the first of a four-semester long design sequence that constitutes the core studio curriculum within the Master of Architecture program at the Weitzman School of Design. This studio introduces specific modes of architectural thinking and practice through a set of projects that examine the design of civic space. The semester includes research into the evolution of the art museum alongside projects that operate across a range of scales, from objects and furniture to institutional space. Through these projects, students examine architectural history and precedent while developing an understanding of tectonics and material logics. A range of digital design techniques, rigorous architectural drawing and physical model making are used to explore relationships between interior planning, exterior massing with a particular focus on the development of plan and section. The semester culminates in the design of a small art institution, allowing students to bring these foundational concepts together in the development of architectural space. Successful completion of ARCH 5010 is a prerequisite for beginning ARCH 5020. ARCH 5020 must be successfully completed before moving on to ARCH 6010.
